archimedes: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: scientific low-poly model design reference, NOT a specimen photograph. Original three-quarter view of a bounded Archimedes sp. Mississippian colony reconstruction based on Kentucky Geological Survey Breckenridge County fossils with attached mesh fronds. A delicate ivory corkscrew axis, about 35 mm tall, supporting one continuous upward spiraling funnel-like lacy fenestrate frond through 2.5 turns. Thin divergent radial branches connected by tiny transverse crossbars, hundreds of actual open rectangular fenestrules, NOT a solid helicoid ribbon, not a stacked cone toy. Rim gently flares upward, leaving air gaps between turns; inner axial helix visible. Fragile chipped fossil-like ends but no enclosing rock, no pedestal. Original warm ivory and ochre matte faceted style, clean off-white background, subtle shadow, clear 3D depth. No text, labels, decorative stars, plants, tentacles, or copied source imagery. Entire form visible. Scientific boundaries: generic specimen-informed reconstruction, exact complete colony and dimensions artistic.
penniretepora: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: original scientific low-poly model design reference. Show a tiny Penniretepora flexistriata colony fragment reconstructed from published SNSB-BSPG 2020 XCI 121/122 SEM morphology, front three-quarter macro view on off-white background. A straight slender main branch 0.32 mm wide and 6.2 mm long, carrying 8 alternating pairs of narrow unconnected lateral branches, each 0.18 mm wide and ~1.3 mm long, spaced 0.72 mm along the main axis and diverging at 70 degrees. Overall resembles a delicate fishbone, never leaf blade or mesh. Do not join side branches to each other. On the same front-facing surface of the main and each lateral branch show two rows of small recessed circular apertures separated by a low subtly undulating median keel, no keel nodes. Apertures only 0.07 mm wide, believable ratios, do not enlarge them. Low-poly warm muted tan calcitic fossil material, real thick 3D branches, no plant leaves, no coral polyps, no rock base, no text. The repeated branch length is a bounded artistic extrapolation, source is a fossil fragment.
constellaria: Use case: stylized-concept. Original scientific educational low-poly design. Constellaria florida fossil colony fragment, based on OUIP 24 from Kope Formation Franklin County Indiana. Broad flattened calcitic branching frond forming an irregular open Y, broad arms 12 mm across and 3.5 mm thick, about 48 mm tall, cut/broken terminal ends and no rock. The two broad surfaces bear shallow stellate maculae as integrated depressed radiating channels with close small pore rows on slightly raised intervening skeletal ridges. The stars are subtle organically embedded topography, NOT raised starfish glued on and NOT decorative gold stars. Visible irregular five/six/radial depressions blend smoothly into branch surface. Warm pale limestone and subtle tan crevices, low-poly faceted silhouette, a sparse aperture pattern, thickness clearly visible at a side angle. Off-white studio, whole fossil visible, no labels or text, no tentacles or biological soft tissue. Nominal dimensions and arrangement artistic but retain source-supported broad flattened branch morphology and depressed stellar relief.
cystodictya: Use case: stylized-concept. Original scientific educational low-poly 3D model concept of Cystodictya formosa, based on published SNSB-BSPG 2020 XCI 99 fossil fragment and XCI 23c cross-section. Bounded reconstructed narrow bifoliate strap-shaped Y branch, NOT a broad leaf coral, about 5 mm tall, each branch 0.88 mm wide and 0.58 mm thick, visible lenticular cross-section. One gently curved lower stem forks into two short narrow free prongs, no network. Exactly five longitudinal alternating aperture rows on BOTH broad faces. Circular/oval aperture diameter around 0.14 mm; small asymmetric horseshoe lunaria at the apertures and faint longitudinal striation. Surface apertures are recessed cavities, not beads. Original pale gray-beige calcitic low-poly fossil, warm ridge highlights, no painted texture, no living polyps, no base or rock. Three-quarter view allows one broad face and side thickness, neutral off-white background. No text. Whole branching arrangement is an explicitly artistic extrapolation from incomplete fossils; do not mix another species anatomy.
